Why you should trust us
Daron DeanI’ve been snorkeling since I was 5, and I am PADI certified. I grew up on the water in Florida, with my mother often having to tell people that, no, it wasn’t a lost life jacket they were seeing — it was her daughter, always floating with a mask, looking at sea creatures. I’ve lived in Florida for 25 years, on and off.
For this guide, I did the following:
I interviewed experts, including Arielle Halford, general manager of Divers Direct, a dive shop located in Key West, Florida.
I sank deep into reviews on YouTube, customer comments on Amazon and other sites, and discussions on dive sites across the internet.
I tested eight snorkel sets with friends in Key West who have been snorkeling and diving for decades in locations such as the Bahamas, Cozumel, the Florida Keys, Jamaica, and Roatán.
For further testing, I took the sets to Ginnie Springs in Central Florida. I swam a length of the springs to test the propulsion of the fins, the comfort of the masks, and the comfort and function of the snorkels.

Who this is for
This guide focuses on snorkel sets for adolescents and adults who are looking to casually snorkel calmer waters, such as springs or rivers or particularly placid ocean locales.
Of course, while traveling, many people rent such equipment — but you might say a hard no to something that has been used by the multitudes and is supposed to go in your mouth. Though renting gear is potentially more affordable, it also limits your options, and you can’t test it in advance to learn whether the mask leaks on your particular face shape, say, or how well the fins fit your feet.
Owning a snorkel set of your own is ideal if you envision yourself doing this more than once or twice in your life. After you take the time to find a set that fits you, you’ll know that it will serve you well whenever you need it.
A basic snorkel set consists of a pair of fins, a mask, a snorkel tube, and a bag to carry all of that. The fins allow you to move more efficiently through the water. The mask and tube allow you to see and breathe while underwater. One end of the snorkel tube fits in your mouth, while the other end sticks up out of the water’s surface, and the snorkel may include contraptions to keep water out and blast it out if it happens to get in.
“The most important thing when it comes to entry-level stuff is getting a good-fitting mask,” said Divers Direct’s Arielle Halford, “because if the mask doesn’t fit right, you’re not going to enjoy your time.”
Though no leaky mask succeeded in earning our recommendation, even with our picks we can’t guarantee a seal for people with facial hair. Whiskers have foiled nearly every mask design, and people rocking a ’stache should use a silicone-based seal in addition to their gear.
Every snorkel we tested has a dry top: When you submerge, a mechanism blocks the flow of water into the snorkel and hence your lungs. This feature can be great for beginners, who are unused to this kind of equipment, or for people who are swimming in choppy water, which tends to splash into the tube. (You wouldn’t want the extra buoyancy if you were planning on freediving or scuba diving.) Just be aware that, as dry-top snorkels include more moving parts, they require more maintenance and create a possible point of failure. Rinse yours in fresh water after every use to prevent corrosion from the sea’s minerals.

   - flights: from "nearby" (all airports near home) unless they chose "Closest only" (then that one airport). Map Layovers to max_layover (nonstop, 5h, 10h, any) and Departure time to depart_times (early_morning, midday, evening, late_night). Don't ask which airport; don't suggest driving.
   - stays: area, check-in/out, guests, nightly budget as max_price (with its currency when they named one, e.g. { amount: 400, currency: "EUR" }); type "hotel" or "rental". When they name hotel brands, a neighborhood or landmark, or a vibe, pass them as wants (brand, area, vibe); if the result says no listing meets the brand, tell them that plainly instead of naming other hotels as matches.
   - weather: trips are outdoors, so check it with start_date/end_date.
   - wikipedia once with every sight or landmark name.
4. Things to do and places to visit: a show_ui cards block with shape "wide", one card per place with a short note, its link, and place ("name, city") for the map link. Hotels and rentals come from the stays card; don't repeat them.
5. Reply with the best flight value and best stay pick in a sentence or two. Booking is theirs: point to the card links.

Mountain View’s Halloween celebration is an activity-packed fall festival with a Treat Trail, food trucks, a bike circus, live performances and more. Courtesy City of Mountain View. Halloween in 2026 can be a frightful enough time without adding fear of missing out into the mix. And with the sheer number of events in Silicon Valley between now and Oct. 31, there’s no shortage of ways to celebrate.
A witch paddle at Pillar Point Harbor, a haunted hangar at Hiller Aviation Museum and “Nightfall” at Filoli are among the many happenings, with events for kids, teens, adults and pets. Check out our monster Halloween events guide before time runs out.
Nightfall at Filoli features numerous settings, including a decorated house and trail, a haunted railway and more. Courtesy Filoli. Family-friendly festivities
Nightfall: The grounds of the Woodside estate transform for the spooky season into a multifaceted, immersive Halloween experience. Find a trail decked out with glowing trees, giant slugs and 1,000 jack-o-lanterns, or a harvest party with food, live music, games and thousands of gourds. New this year are The Haunted Railway with eight miniature trains and The Witches’ Village.
Filoli notes that while some popular dates and times are sold out for general admission, entry is included with tickets for its Champagne Lounge and fire pit experiences.

Halloween Movie Night: Bring lawn chairs and blankets to watch “Maleficent” on the Grant Park soccer field.
Oct. 17, 6:30 p.m., 1575 Holt Ave., Los Altos. Free. losaltosca.gov/739/Halloween-Movie-Night.

Halloween falls on a Saturday this year, the first since 2020, giving us a full weekend to celebrate here in the Santa Clara Valley. And daylight saving time ends early Sunday, Nov. 1 At 2am the clocks go back an hour, so late-nighters get an extra hour of Halloween night this year. Spooky, right?
From haunted mansions and Morgan Hill corn mazes to downtown cocktail nights, Campbell’s costumed street party and Día de los Muertos commemorations around San Jose, here are some options to commune with the living and the dead.
Haunted Houses and Halloween Attractions
Festival Fright Nights at Winchester Mystery House
Select nights through Nov. 1
Sarah Winchester’s estate becomes a walk-at-your-own-pace Halloween festival with four themed zones and 13 attractions, including haunted houses inside the mansion itself. The 2026 storyline is set in 1926, after Sarah Winchester’s death, and add-ons include a flashlight-only Underhouse tour, an attic adventure and a Houdini séance. Recommended for ages 13 and up; tickets start at $59.99 and are sold online only, with prices varying by night.
525 S. Winchester Blvd., San Jose
festivalfrightnights.com

The Bernal Scream
Through Nov. 8
The backyard haunt that father and son Abel and Mike Barrera started in 2013 has grown into one of the South Bay’s biggest commercial scares. For 2026, it opens two haunted attractions under one ticket for the first time in its history. It stays open a week past Halloween for anyone who missed the rush.
Santa Clara County Fairgrounds, 344 Tully Rd., San Jose [This year we will be located in Gateway Hall at Santa Clara County Fairgrounds. Look for the big blue archway, entrance Gate C.]
thebernalscream.com

Dead Time Dreams: The Veil
Through Nov. 1
What could be more spooky than celebrating the holiday in an empty shopping mall parking lot? Dead Time Dreams sets up a haunted attraction built around supernatural creatures and jump scares. A Midway of Terror outside adds roaming characters, live entertainment and nightly shows. Tickets start at $25, and parking is free.
Eastridge Mall, 322 Eastridge Loop, San Jose
deadtimedreams.com

Grimm’s Hollow: Grimm Manor
Select evenings through Oct. 31
Moreland Education Foundation’s pumpkin patch adds Grimm Manor, a family haunted trail where visitors solve clues to escape a cursed estate. After 8:30pm, The Shadows turns up the terror and is not recommended for children under 10. The trail costs $15; community games and movie nights are free, and proceeds fund Moreland School District after-school programs.
Easterbrook Discovery School, 4835 Doyle Rd., San Jose
grimmshollow.com

The Albertson Halloween House
Oct. 31
For its 25th year, an East San Jose family and their neighbors turn a front yard into a walk-through Star Wars: The Mandalorian set, complete with a life-size AT-RT walker and an Armorer’s forge. Costumed characters greet 800 to 1,500 trick-or-treaters each year. Admission is free.
497 N. 16th St., San Jose
albertzone.com/halloween

Pumpkin Patches and Trick-or-Treat Events
Trick or Treat Along Lincoln Avenue
Oct. 30, 11am–12:30pm (toddlers) and 3–4:30pm (school-age kids)
Downtown Willow Glen businesses between Minnesota Avenue and Willow Street hand out candy in two sessions split by age. Organizers ask families to walk the route clockwise.
Lincoln Avenue, San Jose
willowglen.org

Halloween at the Palo Alto Farmers Market
Oct. 31, 8am–12pm
With Halloween on a Saturday, the downtown market folds trick-or-treating, games and a scavenger hunt into its regular morning. Pumpkins are for sale, and kids can guess how many creepy-crawlies fill a jar. Free.
Gillman St, parking lots between Forest Ave. and Hamilton Ave., Palo Alto

Mountain View’s Halloween celebration is an activity-packed fall festival with a Treat Trail, food trucks, a bike circus, live performances and more. Courtesy City of Mountain View. Halloween in 2026 can be a frightful enough time without adding fear of missing out into the mix. And with the sheer number of events in Silicon Valley between now and Oct. 31, there’s no shortage of ways to celebrate.
A witch paddle at Pillar Point Harbor, a haunted hangar at Hiller Aviation Museum and “Nightfall” at Filoli are among the many happenings, with events for kids, teens, adults and pets. Check out our monster Halloween events guide before time runs out.
Nightfall at Filoli features numerous settings, including a decorated house and trail, a haunted railway and more. Courtesy Filoli. Family-friendly festivities
Nightfall: The grounds of the Woodside estate transform for the spooky season into a multifaceted, immersive Halloween experience. Find a trail decked out with glowing trees, giant slugs and 1,000 jack-o-lanterns, or a harvest party with food, live music, games and thousands of gourds. New this year are The Haunted Railway with eight miniature trains and The Witches’ Village.
Filoli notes that while some popular dates and times are sold out for general admission, entry is included with tickets for its Champagne Lounge and fire pit experiences.
Through Nov. 1, times vary, 86 Cañada Road, Woodside. General admission is $45-$55, free for kids 3 and under. Champagne Lounge is $60-$125, free for kids 4 and under. Fire pits are $950 for up to eight guests. filoli.org/whats-on/events/nightfall.
Quoth the Raven Nevermore Terror Tea: By the Teashore in downtown Half Moon Bay is hosting a Halloween-themed afternoon tea. Set in a 1903 Victorian house, almost all the food is made in-house.
Oct. 17-Nov. 1, times vary, 724 Main St., Half Moon Bay. $90 for adults, $55 for kids 12 and under (includes tax and tip). bytheteashore.com.
Freaky Friday Night Flicks: Teens 13-18 can bring a pillow and blanket to watch “Beetlejuice” (Oct. 16), “The Addams Family” (Oct. 23) and “The Nightmare Before Christmas” (Oct. 30) at the Campbell Library. The library will also screen “Poltergeist” for teens and adults on Halloween. Snacks will be provided.
Fridays through Oct. 30 at 4 p.m. and Oct. 31, 3:30-5:30 p.m., 70 N. First St., Campbell. Free. sccl.bibliocommons.com/events/6abc6381377296003a489153. sccl.bibliocommons.com/events/6abc632a377296003a489148.
Halloween Extravaganza: South San Francisco’s Halloween celebration is truly an extravaganza, with a pumpkin patch and a floating pumpkin patch, a pet costume contest, trunk-or-treat, games and a Storybook Walk. There will also be food trucks, a pet adoption tent, a tree giveaway program and flu shot clinic.
Oct. 17, 10 a.m.-2 p.m., Orange Memorial Park, 1 W. Orange Ave., South San Francisco. Free admission; pumpkin activities are $8. Preregistration is required for the pet costume contest and pumpkin patches. ssfca.gov/Departments/Parks-Recreation/Events/Halloween-Extravaganza.
Halloween Movie Night: Bring lawn chairs and blankets to watch “Maleficent” on the Grant Park soccer field.
Oct. 17, 6:30 p.m., 1575 Holt Ave., Los Altos. Free. losaltosca.gov/739/Halloween-Movie-Night.
A costume contest is one of the many happenings at the Half Moon Bay Art & Pumpkin Festival Oct. 17-18. Courtesy Half Moon Bay Art & Pumpkin Festival. Half Moon Bay Art & Pumpkin Festival: Find all things pumpkin at one of the Peninsula’s marquee fall festivals, from the giant pumpkin crowned the winner of Oct. 12’s pumpkin weigh-off to pumpkin patches, food, drinks. Single-day events include the Great Pumpkin Parade, the Pumpkin Run and costume contest. There’s live entertainment, art vendors, pie-eating contests and more throughout the weekend.
Oct. 17-18, 9 a.m.-5 p.m., downtown Half Moon Bay

The OnePlus Nord 5 offers notable improvements over last year's Nord 4 model, including a Snapdragon 8s Gen 3 chipset and enhanced cameras. A key design change is the replacement of the alert slider with a new "Plus Key," which can be remapped for various functions, including the new Plus Mind feature.
The Nord 5 runs OxygenOS 15 based on Android 15, offering AI features like Plus Mind, AI VoiceScribe, AI Call Assistant, and AI Translation. It's slated to receive four years of OS upgrades and six years of security updates. The phone features a glass and metal design with a 6.83-inch screen and a substantial 6,800mAh battery.
It features a Snapdragon 8s Gen 3 SoC from Qualcomm, and the handset is the first Nord series phone with an 8-series chip. While not the latest, it's optimised for smooth day-to-day operation and demanding applications. The 6.83-inch Full-HD+ AMOLED screen refreshes at 144Hz and supports up to 1,800 nits peak brightness.
Camera capabilities include a 50-megapixel primary sensor with OIS, an 8-megapixel ultrawide, and a 50-megapixel selfie camera. The primary camera performs well in various lighting conditions, while the ultrawide is decent when there's enough light. It also supports up to 4K/60fps video recording on the main and selfie cameras.
The 6,800mAh battery is quite reliable, lasting up to a day and a half with moderate usage, and supports 80W SuperVOOC fast charging. Overall, the OnePlus Nord 5 is a strong contender in its price range, offering reliable performance, a good primary camera, optimised software, and long lasting battery life.

turns.text:
**The best all-rounder under ₹30,000 is the Motorola Edge 70 Fusion, but today's Flipkart price puts it just over budget.** The POCO X8 5G is the best pick that actually fits.

- **Motorola Edge 70 Fusion:** Reviewers rank it first for the 7,000mAh battery, curved 144Hz AMOLED screen and clean software. Flipkart lists the 128GB model at ₹30,999. TechVerdict reported about ₹29,300, so a bank offer may bring it under ₹30,000.
- **POCO X8 5G:** It's ₹25,499 on Flipkart and has a 9,000mAh battery. It promises 4 years of OS updates, but the chip is modest and there's no ultrawide camera.
- **OPPO K14 Plus:** Flipkart shows ₹32,999, which is over budget. The ₹29,999 price was for the 6GB model, and it dropped to about ₹25,999 only with a sale bank offer.

None of these phones has a great camera. If photos matter most, you'd need to spend more. Prices change daily, and I didn't find hands-on tests for some of these models. Confirm the exact RAM and storage variant on the listing before you buy.

The OnePlus Nord 5 offers notable improvements over last year's Nord 4 model, including a Snapdragon 8s Gen 3 chipset and enhanced cameras. A key design change is the replacement of the alert slider with a new "Plus Key," which can be remapped for various functions, including the new Plus Mind feature.
The Nord 5 runs OxygenOS 15 based on Android 15, offering AI features like Plus Mind, AI VoiceScribe, AI Call Assistant, and AI Translation. It's slated to receive four years of OS upgrades and six years of security updates. The phone features a glass and metal design with a 6.83-inch screen and a substantial 6,800mAh battery.
It features a Snapdragon 8s Gen 3 SoC from Qualcomm, and the handset is the first Nord series phone with an 8-series chip. While not the latest, it's optimised for smooth day-to-day operation and demanding applications. The 6.83-inch Full-HD+ AMOLED screen refreshes at 144Hz and supports up to 1,800 nits peak brightness.
Camera capabilities include a 50-megapixel primary sensor with OIS, an 8-megapixel ultrawide, and a 50-megapixel selfie camera. The primary camera performs well in various lighting conditions, while the ultrawide is decent when there's enough light. It also supports up to 4K/60fps video recording on the main and selfie cameras.
The 6,800mAh battery is quite reliable, lasting up to a day and a half with moderate usage, and supports 80W SuperVOOC fast charging. Overall, the OnePlus Nord 5 is a strong contender in its price range, offering reliable performance, a good primary camera, optimised software, and long lasting battery life.

turns.text:
**The OnePlus Nord 5 is the best all-rounder near this budget, but Flipkart lists it at ₹31,905, about ₹1,900 over.** Bank offers might bring it under ₹30,000, so check at checkout. Gadgets 360 praises its Snapdragon 8s Gen 3 chip, 144Hz AMOLED screen, OIS main camera and 6,800mAh battery. It also gets 4 OS and 6 years of security updates.

If it has to be under ₹30,000 in sticker price:
- **OnePlus Nord CE6 Lite:** ₹27,749 for the 128 GB model on Flipkart. I didn't find specs or reviews for it, so I can't vouch for it.
- **Realme P4 Power 5G:** about ₹29,930, with a 10,001 mAh battery. That price is indicative, from GSMSpecs. It's the pick if battery life matters most.
- **Motorola Edge 70 Fusion:** ₹30,999 for the 128 GB model on Flipkart, so also slightly over.

GSMSpecs ranks the Pixel 7a first, but it's an older phone. I wouldn't buy it over the Nord 5. Prices change often, so confirm them on the store page before buying.

1. For a recipe or meal, list the ingredients to buy and skip pantry basics (salt, pepper, sugar, oil, water, common dried spices). Scale quantities to the servings.

3. Cart edits: the chat has one cart. For "add tortillas", "drop the cheese", "make it for 6", call shop again with only the new items or remove, and no stores. Pass stores only if they ask for different ones; new_cart only for an unrelated list.
4. A shopping list you write yourself (not from shop) is a cards block with one card per item, even without link or price. Use a checklist only for steps or to-dos.
5. Reply in one or two sentences: the best-value store, how much cheaper than the next, and any missing items. Don't repeat products in show_ui, and never use image_search for product pictures.

# Research and reports 1. Search and read the key sources: up to four web searches (parallel when independent) and six pages. Don't keep searching for marginal gains. Use wikipedia once for people, places, or events. 2. If the subject or options are recognizable by sight (products, cars, places, food, gear, buildings), call image_search once with one query per item, e.g. ["2026 Mazda MX-5 Miata", "Toyota GR86"], unless the pages you read already listed good images. For a quick "tell me about" overview, start the card with an image block from image_search, then the key facts. 3. Something to buy (a phone, an appliance, gear): once you have the top 2-3 picks, call shop once with them at the user's regional default stores, so the report and reply carry live local prices and buy links in their currency. 4. Home

Palo Alto Heat Pump Rebates: The Complete CPAU Guide

BLOG / REBATES
What CPAU pays when you replace a gas heater with a heat pump, which add-ons stack, and the 90-day deadline people miss.By the ComfortFlow teamUpdated October 11, 20265 min read
Call 650-460-3483

City of Palo Alto Utilities offers a Heat Pump HVAC rebate of $2,500, or $5,000 for income-eligible residents, when a heat pump replaces a gas or fossil fuel heater. Add-on rebates cover a qualifying panel upgrade ($1,000, or $2,000 income-eligible) and $500 per qualifying circuit or device. Applications are due within 90 days of final inspection.
Who qualifies
The CPAU Heat Pump HVAC rebate is for City of Palo Alto Utilities residential customers. The key rule is simple: the new heat pump must replace a gas or fossil fuel home heater. Replacing an existing electric heat pump or adding cooling to a home that already heats electrically doesn’t qualify for the core rebate.
If you live in Menlo Park, East Palo Alto, Mountain View, Los Altos or on the Stanford campus, you aren’t a CPAU customer, and different programs apply. See our service area pages for notes on each.
Rebate amounts (as published on the City of Palo Alto Rebate Hub)
RebateStandardIncome-eligibleKey rule
Heat Pump HVAC (core)$2,500$5,000Must replace a gas or fossil fuel heater
Electrical panel upgrade (add-on)$1,000$2,000Paired with a core rebate; new panel 200 amps or less
Panel upgrade permit fee (add-on)Not offered$1,000Income-eligible only
Prewiring, circuit splitter/pauser, subpanel (add-on)$500 each$500 eachMust serve the new heat pump; limits apply

Rebates change. We confirm the current numbers with CPAU before you sign a contract.
How add-ons work
Add-on rebates are not available for standalone projects. They must be paired with a core rebate like Heat Pump HVAC. The wiring add-on is limited to one subpanel rebate and two circuit splitter or pauser rebates per household. If you also replace a gas water heater with a heat pump water heater, that has its own core rebate and separate application.
The steps
Get an assessment. We confirm the existing heater is gas, check the panel, and design the system.
Permit. Most single-family heat pump projects can use the City’s instant permit.
Install and inspect. The project must pass final inspection.
Apply within 90 days of final inspection. This is the deadline people miss most often.

Instant rebates at the point of sale
CPAU lets you receive the rebate at the point of sale when you use a contractor listed as a CPAU Instant Rebate Partner in the City’s Contractor Directory. That means the rebate comes off your invoice instead of arriving later. Ask any contractor whether they participate.
Tips to get the most out of it
Plan the panel early. If your panel needs work, pairing it with the heat pump unlocks the add-on rebate.
Consider load management first. A circuit splitter or pauser may avoid a panel upgrade entirely, and it has its own add-on rebate.
Do the water heater too. Combining a heat pump water heater with a heat pump HVAC project can mean two core rebates and one round of electrical work.
Keep paperwork. Save the permit, final inspection record, invoice and equipment specs.

Ready to plan yours? See heat pump installation in Palo Alto or call us at 650-460-3483.
Example: how the rebates can stack
Here is how a typical Palo Alto project might combine incentives, using the amounts published on the City of Palo Alto Rebate Hub. A homeowner replaces an aging gas furnace and central air conditioner with a ducted heat pump. The project qualifies for the $2,500 Heat Pump HVAC rebate. Their 100-amp panel is tight on capacity, so they add a circuit splitter instead of upgrading the whole panel, which qualifies for a $500 add-on rebate. If the same household also replaces a gas water heater with a heat pump water heater, that is a separate core rebate with its own application.

NEWS / UTILITIES
Palo Alto Utility Rates Rose 8% in July. Gas Rose Fastest.
City Council approved an 8% overall utility increase for the fiscal year starting July 1, 2026. Gas went up twice as much as electricity.By the ComfortFlow teamJune 15, 2026
Call 650-460-3483

On June 15, 2026, the Palo Alto City Council approved an 8% overall utility rate increase for the fiscal year starting July 1, 2026: wastewater 16%, gas 9%, water 8%, electric 4.5% and refuse 3%. The City estimated the change at about $35 per month for the median household, including $7.30 for gas and $4.00 for electricity.
What changed
The City of Palo Alto’s June 2026 bill insert listed the proposed changes, and the Palo Alto Daily Post reported that City Council approved them on June 15, 2026.
Gas rose about twice as fast as electricity in Palo Alto’s July 2026 rate change. UtilityIncreaseMedian monthly change
Wastewater16%$10.70
Gas9%$7.30
Water8%$10.00
Electric4.5%$4.00
Stormwater3%$0.50
Refuse3%$1.50
Total8%$35.20

The City’s gas estimate holds commodity prices constant; actual gas commodity rates change monthly.
What the July 2026 rate change means for a typical Palo Alto household. The longer trend
In April 2026, the Daily Post reported City projections that the average utility bill could rise from $441.50 to about $615.70 per month by 2031. The same report noted that the City transfers 18% of gas revenue to the general fund, and that utilities staff are studying a transition away from gas while still maintaining the gas system.
What it means for heating and cooling
Gas heat costs more each year. With gas rising faster than electricity, furnaces and gas water heaters get more expensive to run relative to heat pumps.
Palo Alto’s electricity is carbon neutral, so a heat pump cuts both cost exposure and emissions.
Rebates offset the upfront cost. CPAU’s Heat Pump HVAC rebate is $2,500, or $5,000 for income-eligible households, when a heat pump replaces gas heat.

Run the numbers for your home with our heat pump cost guide, or see heat pump installation.
A century of city-run gas
Palo Alto has distributed natural gas since 1917, and in October 2022 the City Council set a goal of carbon-neutral gas by 2030. Gas has been carbon neutral through offsets since July 1, 2017, but gas emissions in 2024 were only 34.5% below 1990, far behind the city’s overall progress.

California Rate Relief is a referral service. We are not a licensed contractor. California Rate Relief is compensated by a solar provider when a homeowner we refer signs an agreement. How we make money

Who provides electricity in Palo Alto
CPAU is the City's own utility, and its rate schedules are issued by the City Council rather than set by the CPUC. On the California Energy Commission's utility map, CPAU's territory covers about 99% of Palo Alto's land, with slivers at the edges in PG&E territory; the name on your bill settles it. No community choice provider sits on top, so one utility handles generation, delivery and billing.
Because CPAU is not one of the investor-owned utilities, the CPUC programs built for PG&E, SCE and SDG&E customers, such as CARE, FERA, the Base Services Charge and the Net Billing Tariff, are not how Palo Alto bills work. CPAU has its own bill assistance and its own solar rules, both below.
Read next: The Bay Area cities that run their own utilities

What CPAU charges a home
Schedule E-1 applies to separately metered single-family homes. Each kWh price has three parts. Tier 1 is 10.839 cents for the commodity, 10.024 cents for distribution and 0.631 cents for public benefits, 21.494 cents in all; Tier 2 is 13.973, 9.371 and 0.631 cents, 23.975 cents in all. Tier 1 covers 15 kWh a day, prorated by the days between meter readings, which is 450 kWh in a 30-day bill.
At those prices a 30-day month using 450 kWh comes to about $102 before any taxes or surcharges ($5.38 plus 450 × $0.21494, our arithmetic), and each kWh above Tier 1 adds about 24 cents. A voluntary time-of-use schedule, E-1-TOU, is open to homes with an advanced meter, but not to net-metered solar customers.
For scale, the CPUC Public Advocates Office put PG&E's residential average rate at 33.7 cents per kWh in June 2026. That is a class-wide average rather than a tier price, but it shows why a Palo Alto quote should never be built on PG&E's rates.

Help with the bill, and solar
CPAU's Rate Assistance Program takes 35% off electricity charges, and 25% off gas, for households with a physician-certified medical need or income up to 80% of the area median: as of July 1, 2026, $113,700 a year for one person and $162,400 for a household of four.
New solar customers are on CPAU's NEM 2 program, which began when the original program reached its 10.8 MW cap at the end of 2017. NEM 2 customers are paid for exported electricity under Schedule E-EEC-1: $0.0990 per kWh from July 1, 2026, less than half the E-1 tier prices, so power used at home as it is produced is worth more than power sent to the grid.

args.title: Heat pump vs gas furnace: 1,800 sq ft Palo Alto home
args.html:
HOME HEATING · PALO ALTO, CA · CPAU CUSTOMERS

Choose a heat pump, unless your AC and furnace are both brand new

Mild Bay Area winters, a $2,500 city rebate, and gas rates rising faster than electric tip the math toward a ducted heat pump.

Verdict: heat pump. In Palo Alto's mild climate a heat pump needs no gas backup. It replaces both furnace and AC, so after the city rebate it costs about the same as furnace + AC. It is also exposed to the faster-rising gas rates less. If only the furnace is failing and your AC is under about 8 years old, a new furnace is cheaper up front.
$2,500CPAU rebate (up to $5,000 income-eligible)
$0Federal 25C credit (ended 12/31/2025)
+9% / +4.5%Gas vs electric rate rise, July 2026
21.5¢/kWhCPAU E-1 Tier 1 electric rate

Part 1

Upfront cost

These are national typical ranges for a ~2,000 sq ft home with existing ducts. They are not Palo Alto quotes. Bay Area labor, permits and panel work often push costs toward the high end, so get local quotes.

SystemTypical installedNotes
Ducted heat pump (heat + cool)$12,000–$18,000One system replaces furnace and AC
Gas furnace (96% AFUE)$5,000–$9,000Heating only
Central AC (16 SEER2)$4,000–$8,000Cooling only
Furnace + AC$9,000–$17,000The fair comparison to a heat pump

Net installed cost range, high end (after Palo Alto's $2,500 rebate)

Heat pump, net$15,500
Furnace + AC$17,000
Furnace only$9,000

Low-end net: heat pump about $9,500 vs furnace + AC about $9,000. The two are roughly even once the rebate is applied.

Part 2

Efficiency

Heat pump

  • Moves heat instead of making it: seasonal COP of about 3–4 (300–400%)
  • Does best at 40–60°F, which is typical Bay Area weather
  • Cooling comes with it, so you don't need a separate AC

Gas furnace

  • Max about 96–98% AFUE, so it can't beat 100%
  • Burns gas indoors, with combustion and venting
  • Needs a separate AC for cooling

Part 3

Running cost

Palo Alto electric (E-1, effective July 1, 2026) is a $5.38 monthly charge plus 21.494¢/kWh for the first 15 kWh a day and 23.975¢ above that. Heat delivered by a heat pump costs electric rate × 29.3 kWh per therm ÷ COP. The table below is my own arithmetic at the Tier 1 rate.

Seasonal COPHeat pump cost per therm of heatGas price at which a 96% furnace costs the same
3.0$2.10$2.01/therm
3.5$1.80$1.73/therm
4.0$1.57$1.51/therm
I couldn't pull the current CPAU gas rate per therm. Check your latest bill. If your all-in gas price is above the right-hand column, the heat pump is cheaper to run for heating. It also removes AC electricity from a separate unit and the gas service charge if you remove the meter.

Palo Alto gas rose 9% in July 2026 against 4.5% for electric, and the city is studying a transition away from gas. That trend favors electric over the system's 15–20 year life. Gas commodity rates reset monthly.

Part 4

Incentives (as of Oct 2026)

ProgramAmountKey rule
CPAU Heat Pump HVAC$2,500 (income-eligible: $5,000)Must replace a gas or fossil heater
Panel upgrade add-on$1,000 ($2,000 income-eligible)Must be paired with the core rebate
Circuit splitter / pauser / subpanel / prewiring$500 eachLimits apply; may avoid a panel upgrade
Gas meter removalUp to $2,500Separate program on the Rebate Hub
Heat pump water heater$3,500 (replacing gas)Separate application; bundle with HVAC
Federal 25C creditExpiredNot available for installs after 12/31/2025

Palo Alto's rebates come from the city utility, not PG&E or neighboring community-choice programs. Rebate figures here come from a local installer's summary of the City's Rebate Hub, so confirm them on the City page before signing. You can get the rebate at point of sale through a CPAU Instant Rebate Partner. Otherwise apply within 90 days of final inspection.

Part 5

Pros and cons at a glance

Heat pump wins when

  • You want AC or your AC is aging
  • You plan to stay 5+ years
  • You can stack rebates (panel, water heater, meter removal)

Furnace wins when

  • Only the furnace failed and the AC is new
  • Your electrical panel needs a costly upgrade
  • You'll sell within 2–3 years

Next steps

What to do

  1. Look up your gas $/therm and annual therms on recent bills.
  2. Get 2–3 quotes: one heat pump, one furnace + AC. Ask each about the CPAU Instant Rebate and whether they size the system with a load calculation (Manual J).
  3. Have your panel capacity checked. A circuit splitter may avoid an upgrade.
  4. Bundle a heat pump water heater to get its own $3,500 rebate with one round of electrical work.
  5. Keep the permit, final inspection record and invoice, and apply within 90 days of inspection.

What is left is smaller, more local and more rule-bound, but it is real money if you plan for it.
This page is our running status check on every program a California homeowner is likely to hear about, written from the programs' own pages rather than from other contractors' blogs. For the full winter heating picture, including the Bay Area's new rules on gas furnaces, see our Winter Heating Help Center.
What has closed

TECH Clean California (single-family heat pump HVAC)Fully reserved since 14 November 2025; not accepting new reservations (TECH Clean California).
HEEHRA (the state's federally funded home electrification rebates)Single-family rebates fully reserved statewide; waitlist only (California Energy Commission).

Heat Pump vs. Gas Furnace: What a Palo Alto Winter Really Costs to Heat

BLOG / UTILITY BILLS
Heat Pump vs. Gas Furnace: What a Palo Alto Winter Really Costs to Heat
We ran the numbers on October 2026 CPAU rates for three Palo Alto homes. The answer depends on your furnace, your winter therms and which tier you land in.By the ComfortFlow teamUpdated October 19, 20266 min read
Call 650-460-3483

On October 2026 City of Palo Alto Utilities rates, delivering one therm of heat costs about $2.10 to $2.34 with a heat pump (COP 3), $2.14 with a 95% gas furnace, $2.55 with an 80% furnace in Tier 1 gas, and about $7.02 with an electric space heater. For a typical home using 51 therms in a winter month, a heat pump roughly breaks even with gas. For larger, older homes whose winter gas use runs into Tier 2, a heat pump can save roughly $80 to $120 a month on heating.
The short answer
It depends on three things: how efficient your current furnace is, how many therms you use in winter, and whether your bill crosses CPAU’s Tier 2 line. We used City of Palo Alto Utilities rates for October 2026 and real Palo Alto usage figures to work it out. These are our calculations, and we show every assumption so you can redo them with your own bills, or try our heat pump calculator.
Cost to put 100,000 Btu of heat into your rooms, October 2026 CPAU rates. The rates we used

Gas commodity prices change monthly, so winter gas prices may be higher or lower than October’s. Electric rates are fixed until the next rate change.
Cost per unit of heat
To compare fairly, we price the same 100,000 Btu (one therm) of heat delivered to your rooms. A gas furnace loses some heat up the flue: an 80% furnace delivers 80% of the gas it burns. A heat pump moves heat instead of making it; NEEP field measurements of variable-speed heat pumps at 47°F ranged from a COP of about 1.9 to 3.9, so we use 3 as typical and 2.5 as a cautious case. Electric resistance heat, like a plug-in space heater, has a COP of 1.

args.title: Heat pump vs gas furnace: 1,800 sq ft home in Palo Alto
args.html:
HOME HEATING · PALO ALTO, CA · OCT 2026

Choose a heat pump, unless your furnace is new and efficient

Running costs are roughly equal to a modern gas furnace. A heat pump wins on a $2,500 city rebate, built-in AC and the coming Bay Area gas-furnace rules.

Heat pump for most Palo Alto homeowners. If you are replacing an old furnace (80% or less) or you want AC, it costs about the same or less to run. A city rebate of up to $2,500 closes most of the upfront gap. Keep a gas furnace only if yours is a recent 95% unit that works well and you don't want AC.
$2,500City of Palo Alto heat pump HVAC rebate ($5,000 if income-eligible)
~300%Heat pump efficiency (COP 3) vs 80–95% for furnaces
$0Federal tax credit in 2026 (25C ended Dec 31, 2025)

Part 1

Upfront cost

These are typical Bay Area ranges from a local HVAC contractor's guide, not quotes. Your ducts, electrical panel and permit needs can move them a lot. Get 2–3 quotes.

Typical installed cost (high end of range)

Gas furnace$3,500–$7,500
Heat pump (before rebate)$5,000–$12,000
Heat pump after $2,500 rebate$2,500–$9,500

The furnace price does not include AC. A heat pump heats and cools, so you avoid buying a separate AC unit. Costs go up if your electrical panel needs an upgrade. Palo Alto has add-on rebates for panel upgrades and insulation, but only when they are bundled with a heat pump project.

Part 2

Efficiency and running cost

A furnace burns gas and loses some heat up the flue: 80% for a standard unit, 95% for a high-efficiency one, and 56–70% for very old units. A heat pump moves heat instead of making it. Field measurements of variable-speed units at 47°F ranged from a COP of about 1.9 to 3.9, and 3 is a typical value. Palo Alto's mild climate suits heat pumps well.

SystemCost per therm of heat delivered*
Heat pump, COP 3 (electric Tier 1 / Tier 2)$2.10 / $2.34
Heat pump, COP 2.5 (Tier 2)$2.81
95% gas furnace (gas Tier 1 / Tier 2)$2.14 / $3.92
80% gas furnace (gas Tier 1 / Tier 2)$2.55 / $4.66
Plug-in electric heater$7.02

*Estimates by a Palo Alto HVAC contractor (ComfortFlow) using City of Palo Alto Utilities rates in Oct 2026. Electricity is 21.5¢/kWh for the first 15 kWh a day and 24¢ above that. Gas is $2.04/therm for the first 60 therms a month in winter and $3.72 above that.

Winter-month heating cost, 80% furnace vs heat pump (Tier 2 electricity)

Large older home (120 therms) · furnace$321
Large older home · heat pump$202–$243
Median home (70 therms) · furnace$135
Median home · heat pump$109–$130
Palo Alto has its own utility, so PG&E rate comparisons don't apply to you. Gas Tier 2 is what makes a furnace expensive for large or drafty homes. If you already have a 95% furnace, the heat pump costs about the same or slightly more to run in small and mid-size homes. Removing gas entirely also saves the $22.41 monthly gas service charge (about $269 a year), but only if the water heater and stove go electric too.

Part 3

Incentives (as of Oct 2026)

ProgramStatusAmount
City of Palo Alto Utilities heat pump HVAC rebateOpenUp to $2,500, or up to $5,000 if income-eligible
CPAU add-ons (insulation, panel upgrade)Open, bundled onlyOnly with a heat pump HVAC, heat pump water heater or induction project
Gas meter removal incentiveOpenTaxable income. Amount not confirmed
Federal 25C tax creditEnded Dec 31, 2025None for 2026 installs
TECH Clean CaliforniaFully reserved since Nov 2025None
State HEEHRA rebatesWaitlist onlyNone
PG&E / BayREN Home+No heat pump rebates listedNone
New gas furnaceNo rebate foundNone

Palo Alto's rules:

  • Use a contractor marked City of Palo Alto Instant Rebate in the Rebate Hub directory. They take the rebate off your invoice at sale and file the paperwork.
  • Rebates need active Palo Alto electric and gas accounts. Reserve the rebate before you install. The City typically approves reservations within 5 business days.
  • Submit the final application within 90 days of passing final inspection. The check arrives about 5 weeks later.

Part 4

Pros and cons

Heat pump

  • Heating and AC in one unit
  • About $2,500 city rebate (more if income-eligible)
  • Cheaper to run than an old or large-home furnace
  • Ready for the Bay Area zero-NOx furnace rule (2029, per a local contractor)
  • Can let you drop the gas meter
  • Higher upfront cost, even after the rebate
  • May need a panel or duct upgrade
  • No savings against a new 95% furnace in a small home

Gas furnace

  • Lowest upfront price
  • Fast, simple swap if the ducts and panel are fine
  • Fine if you already have a good 95% unit
  • No rebate or tax credit
  • Tier 2 gas gets expensive in big or drafty homes
  • Needs separate AC
  • Keeps the $269-a-year gas service charge

Next steps

What to do

  1. Check your last winter gas bills. If you went above 60 therms a month, a heat pump looks better.
  2. Pick a CPAU Instant Rebate contractor from the City's Rebate Hub and get 2–3 quotes. Ask about the panel and duct work and the efficiency rating.
  3. Reserve the rebate before any work starts.
  4. Plan the swap for spring or summer. Rushing in during a January failure can cost you the rebate.
Several figures come from contractor blogs, including the cost ranges, the per-therm math and the 2029 rule. Check the rebate amounts and the rule on the City and Bay Area Air District pages before you sign.

turns.text:
I planned Fri–Sun, Nov 6–8, based in South Lake Tahoe. I searched stays for only 2 nights, Nov 6–8, so tell me if you want a third night. Saturday looks like the best outdoor day (dry, up to 54°F). Friday morning will be below freezing, so check road conditions before you drive.

For stays, Hilton Vacation Club Tahoe Seasons is a good value at $102/night and 4.2/5 on Google. For a cozy cabin, the Airbnb with the hot tub is $300/night and rated 4.89. Booking is up to you through the card links.
